sanskrit: naktaṃjātāsy oṣadhe rāme kṛṣṇe asikni ca | idaṃ rajani rajaya kilāsaṃ palitaṃ ca yat ||
english: You are born of the night, O herb — in the dark, in the black, in the deep-dark. O Rājanī, stain and color away this leprosy (kilāsa) and this greyness (palita).

sanskrit: kilāsaṃ ca palitaṃ ca nir ito nāśayā pṛṣat | ā tvā svo aśnutāṃ varṇaḥ parā śvetāni pātaya ||
english: Both the white-spot disease (kilāsa) and the greyness (palita) — drive them out and destroy them from here, O speckled one. Let your own (natural) color restore itself to you; expel the white patches far away.

sanskrit: asitaṃ te pralayanam āsthānam asitaṃ tava | asikny asy oṣadhe nir ito nāśayā pṛṣat ||
english: Dark (asita) is your place of dissolution, dark (asita) is your abode. You are the dark-herb (asiknī), O plant — drive out and destroy this from here, O speckled one.

sanskrit: asthijasya kilāsasya tanūjasya ca yat tvaci | dūṣā kṛtasya brahmaṇā lakṣma śvetam anīnaśam ||
english: The white mark (śveta lakṣma) upon the skin — whether of leprosy (kilāsa) born from the bones, or born of the body — though wrought by a curse (brahmaṇā dūṣā), I have destroyed it utterly.

sanskrit: jarāyujaḥ prathama usriyo vṛṣā vātabhrajā stanayann eti vṛṣṭyā | sa no mṛḍāti tanva ṛjugo rujan ya ekam ojas tredhā vicakre ||
english: The first-born of the womb, the bull of the dawn-rays (usriya), the cloud-born, goes forth thundering with rain. May he, who moves straight and pierces, whose single vital power (ojas) he has spread threefold, be merciful to our bodies.

sanskrit: aṅgeaṅge śociṣā śiśriyāṇo yo agrabhīt parur asya grabhītā | aṅkān samaṅkān haviṣā yajāmi hṛdi śrito manasā yo jajāna ||
english: He who has lodged himself with blazing flame in every limb, who seized it — the one who seized the joints is also seized. I worship with oblation (havis) the joints and the inter-joints; him who abides in the heart and was born through the mind I worship.

sanskrit: muñcāmi śīrṣaktyā uta kāsa enaṃ paruṣparur āviveśa yo asya | yo abhrajā vātajā yaś ca śuṣmo vanaspatīn sacatāṃ parvatāṃś ca ||
english: I release him from headache and likewise from cough — him who has entered joint by joint. That (affliction) which is cloud-born, which is wind-born, and that parching fever (śuṣma) — let them attend to the forest trees and the mountains.

sanskrit: śaṃ te parasmai gātrāya śam astv avarāya te | śaṃ te pṛṣṭibhyo majjabhyaḥ śam astu tanve tava ||
english: Auspicious (śam) be it for your upper limb, auspicious be it for your lower limb; auspicious be it for your back and your marrows — auspicious be it for your body.

sanskrit: ā yātu mitra ṛtubhiḥ kalpamānaḥ saṃveśayan pṛthivīm usriyābhiḥ | tad asmabhyaṃ varuṇo vāyur agnir bṛhad rāṣṭraṃ saṃveśyaṃ dadhātu ||
english: May Mitra come near, ordering himself by the seasons, settling the earth with the dawn-cows (usriyā). May Varuṇa, Vāyu, and Agni bestow upon us that great kingdom (bṛhad rāṣṭra) worthy of being established.

sanskrit: dhātā mitro varuṇo devo agnir indras tvaṣṭā prati gṛhṇantu me vacaḥ | huve devīm aditiṃ śūraputrāṃ sajātānāṃ madhyameṣṭhāḥ syām aham ||
english: May Dhātṛ, Mitra, Varuṇa, divine Agni, Indra, and Tvaṣṭṛ accept my words. I call upon the goddess Aditi, mother of heroes — may I stand foremost among those born of the same kind (sajāta).

sanskrit: huve somaṃ savitāraṃ namobhir viśvān devām̐ ahamuttaratve | ayam agnir dīdāyad āhnam eva sajātair iddho apratibruvadbhiḥ ||
english: With reverences I call upon Soma and Savitṛ, (and) all the gods, for my own supremacy (uttaratva). This Agni blazes on throughout the day, kindled by the companions of the same birth (sajāta) who do not contradict.

sanskrit: ihed asātha na puro gamātha- -iryo gopāḥ puṣṭapatir va ājat | asmai vaḥ kāmāyopa kāminīr viśve vo devā upa saṃ dyām iha ||
english: Remain here; do not go forward. Ārya, the herdsman and lord of prosperity (puṣṭapati), has driven you (here). Toward him, O desiring-women (kāminī), for his desire — may all the gods bring you (wives) together, here, under the sky.
